sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: An ERM is a fibrocellular proliferation on the inner surface of the internal limiting membrane (ILM). Pathophysiology involves the migration of glial cells (Müller cells), RPE cells, and hyalocytes through retinal breaks or via a posterior vitreous detachment (PVD) creating a scaffold for contraction, leading to macular surface distortion, striae, and pseudo-hole formation.

sections.title: Red Flags & Urgent Findings
content: Rapid vision loss (rule out macular edema/tractional detachment)
Presence of full-thickness macular hole (FTMH) associated with ERM

rows: Cellophane maculopathy: thin, transparent, no distortion
Macular pucker: thick, opaque membrane with severe distortion

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup
content: Step 1: BCVA and Amsler Grid (Metamorphopsia assessment)
Step 2: Dilated Fundoscopy (Observe sheen, striae, and vascular tortuosity)
Step 3: OCT Macula (Gold standard: check for ectopic inner foveal layers, Foveal contour, CMT)
Step 4: Fluorescein Angiography (If secondary cause like RVO is suspected)

sections.title: Surgical Technique: Membrane Peel
content: 3. Staining: Use Triamcinolone (Triesence) or Brilliant Blue G (ILM blue) for visualization
4. Delamination: Use microforceps to grasp membrane edge and peel
5. ILM Peeling: Recommended to prevent recurrence (peel 2-3 disc diameters)

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Visual acuity of 20/40 or worse is a general threshold for surgery.
Metamorphopsia is a better surgical indication than just visual acuity.
ERM recurrence after ILM peeling is significantly lower (<5%).
Expect improvement to be gradual over 3-6 months post-op.
